plan.summary: When a HubSpot contact's lifecycle stage becomes customer, create a Stripe customer record with the contact's email and full name.

The contact has both firstname and lastname properties populated, or name can be constructed from them.
The Stripe API key used has permission to create customers.
No duplicate customer check is required; the integration will create a new Stripe customer each time the trigger fires.

Create a customer | Stripe API Reference

notes: HubSpot sends webhooks as POST requests to a configured URL when contact properties change. The payload includes subscriptionType, propertyName, propertyValue, objectId (contact ID), and portalId. To get firstname, lastname, and email, the connector must make a follow-up GET request to /crm/v3/objects/contacts/{objectId}?properties=email,firstname,lastname,lifecyclestage. The webhook alone does not contain the full contact properties.
The lifecyclestage property uses internal values; 'customer' is a valid internal value for the lifecycle stage enumeration.
HubSpot requires SSL/TLS for webhook endpoints and verifies signatures via the X-HubSpot-Signature header (not shown in docs but required for security).
The contact ID (objectId) is a numeric string; use it to fetch the contact via the CRM API.
Stripe API expects form-encoded data (application/x-www-form-urlencoded), not JSON. The connector must encode the parameters accordingly.
The 'name' parameter combines firstname and lastname from HubSpot (e.g., 'Jane Doe'). If either is missing, use the available part or leave blank.
Email must be present and valid; Stripe enforces a max length of 512 characters.
No idempotency key is used in the example, but it is recommended to prevent duplicate customers on retries.
The test API key (sk_test_) must be replaced with a live key in production. The connector should use environment variable STRIPE_API_KEY.
Stripe returns the full customer object on success; the connector only needs to store the 'id' for future reference if needed.
